posts.title: What is Drawing?
posts.description: See more of my drawing here For some time now I have been thinking about writing a book about drawing. And now, I have decided that I am going to do it. I have been drawing as long as I can remember. All my life. For hours days weeks moments minutes decades. With a pencil in my hand, it is a subject I know very well. But I know it in a way I know breathing or eating – there is little I could express in words. I know it so well, yet don’t know what I think about it. I don’t fully know what it is. Like many others, I write to discover what I think: I want to write a book about drawing to uncover it, to learn about it, to unpick the instinct that comes from a lifetime of wordless application, to discover the knowledge I have and all I do not yet have. There is so much still to find out: The impetus to make marks – be it on a screen, a page, a clay tablet, a cave wall. posts.title: Granular, Diverse, Mainstream, Messy, Normal
posts.description: All of us know a family with an extraordinary story. Searching for the unusual we never have to look far. All lives, at least in moments, are unpredictable, varied and strange. For all that we can easily identify the patterns and shared experiences uniting us, much of what we see and do falls into the category of the unexpected. And the same goes for the types, the characters inhabiting our world. Real souls who would be presumed invention were they written in a book. People may loosely conform to patterns but all have foibles and eccentricities. We are not in any way perturbed by this, for all it takes is the most cursory overview to confirm that it is so. There are many characters who, by temperament, habit, taste and experience, loosely occupy what we call the mainstream. If we were to amalgamate and average them out, we would be close to what is commonly known as normal. Perhaps this is useful, but not nearly so much as we are used to pretending. posts.title: Banned Books – Alert! Alert! Freaks and Weirdos and Scary Ideas!
posts.description: I wrote this essay for Dorset Eye as a part of their recent Banned Books Week focus. In a mindless scroll through social media yesterday, due, I hasten to add, to a friend’s indignation rather than my own preferences, I accidentally noticed ex-footballer Joey Barton. Joey Barton, found guilty earlier this year of kicking his wife in the head, is of the opinion that women playing football is bad because REAL women don’t WANT to play football. A few listless sweeps later and there’s some preppy dude, a ‘right wing commentator’, explaining what REAL Englishness constitutes, how that means, truthfully and scientifically, that Englishness is and can only ever be, a special prize for white people. Surprise surprise. What both these boys made me think was how desperate they and so many others are to define, delineate, tick-box the world, then exclude everything and everyone that can’t or won’t fit inside the thick, crayon lines of their boxes.
